en.title: Set up your first care circle
en.summary: A care circle is a private space for one person you care for. Create an account, choose who you are caring for, type their name and tap "Create circle". It takes about a minute and is free.
steps: Download CircleCare on your iPhone or Android phone and tap "Get started" to create your account.
Under "Who are you caring for?", choose "A parent", "My spouse / partner", "My child", "Myself" or "Someone else".
Type their name or what you call them, like Mom or Grandpa. Adding a date of birth is optional.
Tap "Create circle".
Pick a first step: add a medication, an appointment, invite someone or add emergency info. You can also tap "Skip for now" and come back later.
en.body:
## Were you invited by someone?

If a family member already set up a circle and invited you, **do not create a new one**. Open the invite link from your email instead, or tap "Have an invite code?". If an invitation is waiting for you, the "Create circle" screen shows a banner that says "You have 1 pending invitation". Tap "Review invitation" to join. See [Join a circle you were invited to](/help/join-a-circle/).

## Good to know

- One circle is for one person. If you care for both parents, see [Care for more than one person](/help/second-circle/).
- Choosing "Myself" makes a circle for your own care. You are both the owner and the care recipient, and you can still invite family to help.
- After your first circle, the app may show the Premium plans once. You can tap "Continue with free plan" and keep using CircleCare for free.
- You can also create a circle on a computer at my.circlecare.app: click "Create circle" on your list of circles. See [Use CircleCare on a computer](/help/use-on-a-computer/).

## What to do next

1. [Add a medication and its reminders](/help/add-a-medication/).
2. [Invite family and caregivers](/help/invite-family/).
3. [Keep emergency info and share a care summary](/help/care-info-and-summary/).

en.title: Invite family and caregivers
en.summary: The circle owner invites people by email from the circle's Home screen. They get an email with a link and a 6-character code, and joining is always free for them.
steps: Open the circle and stay on the "Home" tab.
Scroll to "Care team" and tap "Add family member".
Under "Who are you inviting?", choose "Family caregiver" or "Care recipient".
Type their email address and tap "Send invitation".
Optional: tap "Share invite link" or "Copy link" to send the link by text message or chat, so they can join right away.
en.body:
## What the invited person gets

CircleCare emails them a link and an invite code. When they open the link on a phone with CircleCare installed, the app opens. Without the app, the link opens in their web browser, and they can join there. They need a free account. See [Join a circle you were invited to](/help/join-a-circle/).

## Caregiver or care recipient

- **Family caregiver** is for siblings, partners, friends or paid helpers who help with care.
- **Care recipient** is the person being cared for. They get a simpler app focused on medication reminders, and they can confirm when they have taken a dose. A circle can have only one care recipient. The care recipient does not need an account for the circle to work.

## Limits on the free plan

- A free circle includes you plus 1 caregiver. A pending invitation holds that spot until it is accepted, cancelled or expires.
- If the spot is taken by a pending invite, the app shows "Your invitation is already in use". Cancel that invitation to free the spot, or upgrade.
- Inviting the care recipient is never limited. They do not count toward the caregiver limit.
- With Premium, you can invite as many caregivers as you need. See [What is free and what Premium adds](/help/free-and-premium/).

## Pending invitations

Invitations last 7 days. Under "Care team", "Pending invitations" shows each one and when it expires. Once an invitation has expired, tap "Resend" to send it again for another 7 days. To withdraw one, tap the X next to it.

## Good to know

- Only the circle owner and managers can invite people. Other caregivers cannot send invitations. See [Owners, caregivers, care recipients and view-only](/help/roles-and-permissions/).
- On a computer at my.circlecare.app, open the circle, choose "Members" and then "Invite member".

en.title: Join a circle you were invited to
en.summary: Open the invite link from your email and follow the steps to create a free account. You will join the circle straight away. Joining someone else's circle is always free.
steps: Find the invitation email from CircleCare. Check your spam or promotions folder if you do not see it.
Tap the link in the email. If CircleCare is on your phone, the app opens. If not, the invitation opens in your web browser.
In the app, the "Enter your invite code" screen opens with your code filled in. Type the email address the invite was sent to and tap "Continue".
Check who invited you, then tap "Continue to create account" in the app, or "Create an account to join" in the browser.
Create your account. In the app, tap "Create account and join".
If you already have an account, choose "Sign in" (or "I already have an account" in the browser). You join the circle as soon as you sign in.
en.body:
## If you only have the code

The invitation email also includes a 6-character code. Open the app and tap "Have an invite code?", then "Enter code". Type the email address the invite was sent to and the code. On a computer at my.circlecare.app, choose "Join with an invite code".

## If the app asks you to create a circle

After you sign up, the app may show the "Create circle" screen. If someone invited you, **you do not need your own circle**.

- Look for the banner "You have 1 pending invitation" at the top and tap "Review invitation", then "Accept".
- Or tap "Have an invite code?" at the bottom of the screen and type your code.

## If you already made a circle by mistake

Your invitation still works. On your list of circles, tap the pending invite card ("Tap to review and join circles") and accept it. On a computer, go to "Your invitations".

Then you can delete the extra circle: open it, go to "Manage" and tap "Delete circle". A deleted circle does not count toward your free circle, so you can still start your own circle later.

## If the invite does not work

- Invitations last 7 days. If yours has expired, ask the person who invited you to tap "Resend" or send a new invite.
- To join from the list of pending invitations, sign in with the email address the invite was sent to. If you use a different email (for example "Hide My Email" with Apple), use the invite link or the code instead.

## Good to know

- Being invited never costs anything, on the free plan or on Premium. Only the circle owner can pay for Premium.
- You can belong to several circles, for example your mom's circle and your dad's circle.

en.title: Owners, caregivers, care recipients and view-only
en.summary: Each circle has one owner, who created it. Caregivers can see and update care information. A manager is a caregiver who can also invite and remove people. The care recipient gets reminders and confirms their doses. View-only means you can see everything but not make changes.
en.body:
## Circle owner

The person who created the circle. The owner can invite people, cancel or resend invitations, and remove members, and is the only one who can:

- change the circle's details (**Edit circle**)
- delete the circle (**Delete circle**)
- choose who gets medication reminders
- make or remove a manager
- pay for Premium for the circle

## Manager

A manager is a caregiver the owner has chosen to help run the circle. Managers can:

- invite people, and resend or cancel any pending invitation
- see the pending invitations
- remove caregivers from the circle (never the owner or another manager)
- put someone else on a care shift or take someone off one (see [Plan who is on care shifts](/help/care-shifts/))

Managers cannot change the circle's details, delete the circle, choose who gets medication reminders, handle billing, or make other managers. A circle can have more than one manager.

To make someone a manager, the owner opens the circle, taps the person in the list of members (on the web, uses the menu on their row in **Members**), and chooses **Make manager**. To undo it, choose **Remove as manager**. The person stays in the circle as a caregiver.

Good to know:

- Managers are a Premium feature. It follows the owner's plan, so only the owner needs Premium. If the owner's Premium ends, every manager goes back to being a caregiver. Invitations they already sent stay valid. If the owner subscribes again, the owner has to choose managers again.
- The care recipient and view-only members cannot be managers.
- Seat limits are still the owner's. On the free plan the circle has room for the owner plus 1 caregiver, whoever sends the invitation.
- A manager sees the manager tools in CircleCare 1.3.0 or later, and on the website. Older app versions show a manager as a regular caregiver.

## Caregiver

Family members and helpers. When you invite someone, this is the **Family caregiver** choice. Caregivers can see and update care information: medications, doses, appointments, tasks, notes, vitals, documents and emergency info. A caregiver can leave a circle at any time with **Leave circle**, at the bottom of Home.

## Care recipient

The person being cared for. If they join with their own account, they get medication reminders and can confirm when they have taken a dose, and the family is notified. A circle has at most one care recipient. They do not count toward the free plan's caregiver limit. In a circle you create for yourself ("Myself"), you are both the owner and the care recipient.

## View-only

A person with view-only access can see everything in the circle but cannot make changes. They see a "You have view-only access" notice, and the **New** button is dimmed. This happens when:

- a free circle has more caregivers than the free plan allows, for example after the owner's Premium ends. The caregiver who joined first keeps editing, and the others become view-only.
- the owner's Premium ended while they had more than one circle. The circles they did not keep become read-only for everyone.

When the owner upgrades again, editing comes back for everyone. Nothing is deleted. See [What is free and what Premium adds](/help/free-and-premium/).

## Where this is enforced

These rules are checked on CircleCare's servers, not only in the app. Someone without permission cannot get around them by using a different device or the website.

en.title: Use CircleCare on a computer
en.summary: Go to my.circlecare.app in any web browser and sign in with the same account you use on your phone. You see the same circles and information. Reminders and alerts only arrive on the phone app.
steps: Open a web browser on your computer and go to my.circlecare.app.
Sign in with the same email, Google or Apple account you use in the phone app.
Your circle opens. If you have more than one, choose it from your list of circles. To get back to that list later, click the circle's name at the top and choose "All circles".
Use the menu on the side to move between Calendar, Medications, Tasks, Notes, Vitals, Documents, Members and more.
en.body:
## What you can do on a computer

Most everyday things: see the calendar, add and edit medications, appointments and tasks, mark doses, write notes, log vitals, upload documents, keep emergency info, invite family from "Members", and manage your notification settings and subscription from "Profile". Anything you change shows up on everyone's phones too.

## What needs the phone app

- **Reminders and alerts.** CircleCare sends them as push notifications to the iPhone and Android app. The website does not deliver reminders. If you want reminders, install the app and turn on notifications. See [Not getting notifications](/help/notifications-not-arriving/).
- **Adding by voice** is only in the phone app.
- **Importing appointments from your phone's calendar** is only in the phone app.
- **Face ID or fingerprint sign-in** is a phone feature.

## Good to know

- Invited family members can join from a browser without installing anything. They still need a free account.
- To switch between circles on the website, click the circle's name at the top, then "All circles".

en.title: Add a medication and its reminders
en.summary: Tap New, choose Medication, enter the name, dose and times, and save. Reminders are on by default, so the right person is reminded at each dose time.
steps: Tap New at the bottom of the screen, then Med.
Type the Medication name and the Dosage (for example, 100mg or 1 tablet).
Under Date & time, pick a time, or tap a common schedule such as Every morning (it also sets Repeat to Daily). Once a time is set, tap Add another dose time for more doses in a day (up to 4).
Under Repeat, choose how often it is taken, such as Daily or Days of the week.
Check Reminders. Enable notifications is on, with At the scheduled time checked, and you can add Earlier reminders.
Tap Create Medication.
en.body:
## Good to know

- **Who gets the reminder.** Dose reminders go to the care recipient. If the circle owner has chosen someone to handle medication reminders for them, that person gets them instead. See [How reminders and missed-dose alerts work](/help/reminders-and-alerts/).
- **More details** holds refills, pharmacy, prescriber and instructions. Turn on **Track refills** to be told when the bottle is running low.
- **Add a photo** of the bottle so everyone can confirm the right pill.
- **Times are in the care recipient's time zone.** If you live somewhere else, the form shows both your time and theirs.
- **If today's time has already passed**, the medication starts with its next scheduled dose. Nothing is recorded for today.
- **Add by voice.** On supported phones, Premium circles can tap **Add by voice** and say the medication. The form fills in, and nothing is saved until you check it and confirm.

## On a computer

On [my.circlecare.app](/help/use-on-a-computer/), open **Medications** and choose **Add medication**. The form has the same fields. Reminders are push notifications, so they only arrive on phones with the CircleCare app installed.

## Limits

- The free plan has no limit on how many medications or reminders you add.
- CircleCare is a tool, not a doctor. It does not check for drug interactions or give dosing advice.

en.title: Medications on certain days or every few days
en.summary: Under Repeat, choose Days of the week for set weekdays, Every 2 days for every other day, or Cycle for patterns like 7 days on, 7 days off.
steps: Tap New, then Med. Enter the name, dose and a time (for example, tap Every evening).
Tap Repeat.
For set weekdays, choose Days of the week, tap the days you need under Repeat on (the start day is already selected), then tap Done.
For every other day, choose Every 2 days.
For on and off patterns, choose Cycle and set the Days on and Days off (they start at 7 and 7).
Add an End date (optional) if the medication stops on a known date, then tap Create Medication.
en.body:
## Repeat options

The Repeat list offers: **Never**, **Daily**, **Every 2 days**, **Weekly**, **Monthly**, **Yearly**, **Cycle** and **Days of the week**. When you add a new medication, it also offers **As needed** for medications with no set times (see [As-needed medications](/help/as-needed-medications/)).

On the web, the same choices are called **Every other day** and **Cycle (days on / off)**.

## Good to know

- **Days of the week** follows the care recipient's time zone.
- **Several doses a day** are set under Date & time with **Add another dose time**, not under Repeat.
- **Leave the end date blank** to keep the medication going until you stop it.
- **A schedule that started on a day can't drop that day later.** To remove it, stop the medication and add it again with the new days.
- There is no "every 3 days" or other custom interval yet. **Cycle** covers most on-and-off patterns.

## Not for meals or routines

Meals, walks and other routines work better as a repeating task. See [Reminders for meals and daily routines](/help/routine-reminders/).

en.title: Mark a dose taken or skipped
en.summary: On Home, tap Take when a dose is given or Skip when it is not. Everyone in the circle sees who marked it and when.
steps: Open Home, where today's doses are listed.
Tap Take on the dose that was given, or Skip if it was not given.
If you tapped by mistake, tap Undo while it shows.
To see who marked it, tap View history, then History.
en.body:
## What each status means

- **Taken**: someone marked it as given.
- **Skipped**: someone marked it as not given. It shows in grey and counts against the adherence rate.
- **Not marked**: nobody marked the dose. CircleCare never decides on its own that a dose was missed. An unmarked dose stays **Not marked** until someone marks it.

## Good to know

- **From a reminder notification** on your phone, you can also tap I took it or Skip.
- A dose that is past its time and not marked yet shows **Overdue**.
- **Anyone in the circle can mark a dose**, except people with view-only access.
- **If two people mark the same dose**, the app shows who marked it first, for example "Already marked taken by Ana at 8:05 AM." You can change the answer, and everyone sees the change in Activity.
- **Older doses** can be marked from the Meds tab or the calendar.
- **Marked doses build the history.** Open the Meds tab to see adherence, or share a [care summary](/help/care-info-and-summary/).

## On a computer

On the web Overview, use **Confirm** or **Skip** next to each dose.

en.title: How reminders and missed-dose alerts work
en.summary: At dose time the care recipient (or the person chosen to handle their reminders) gets a push. If nobody marks the dose, CircleCare follows up at 15 minutes, 30 minutes and 1 hour, reaching more of the circle each time.
en.body:
## The reminder

At the scheduled time, a push notification goes to **one person**:

1. the member the owner chose for **Medication reminders**, if there is one,
2. otherwise the care recipient,
3. otherwise the circle owner.

To choose that member, the owner opens **Home**, taps the person under **Care team**, and taps **Medication reminders** (then **Switch**, if someone else already gets them). A check mark shows who gets them; tap **Medication reminders** again to send them back to the care recipient.

You can also turn on **Earlier reminders**: **24 hours before**, **1 hour before**, **30 minutes before** or **15 minutes before**.

## If nobody marks the dose

| Time after the dose | Who is told |
|---|---|
| 15 minutes | The person who gets the reminders |
| 30 minutes | The caregivers in the circle |
| 1 hour | Everyone in the circle |

The alerts stop as soon as someone marks the dose **Taken** or **Skipped**. CircleCare never marks a dose "missed" by itself: the dose stays **Not marked** until someone marks it. These follow-ups are included on the free plan. People with view-only access don't get reminders or these alerts.

## Quiet hours

During your [quiet hours](/help/quiet-hours/), reminders and earlier reminders are not sent. Missed-dose alerts wait and arrive when quiet hours end, unless the dose was marked in the meantime. If several alerts waited for the same dose, only the latest one arrives.

## Good to know

- **Push only works on phones.** The web app does not send notifications, so install the app on your phone and allow notifications. See [Not getting notifications](/help/notifications-not-arriving/).
- **Turning reminders off for a medication** stops both the reminder and the follow-up alerts for it.
- **To stop dose updates and missed-dose alerts just for you**, go to Profile and turn off **Medications** under Notifications. This does not stop the dose reminders sent to you.

en.title: Stop a medication vs delete it
en.summary: Use Discontinue when a medication is stopped: reminders end right away and its history is kept. Use Delete only for a medication added by mistake.
steps: Open Care, then the Meds tab.
Tap the ... button on the medication.
Tap Discontinue to stop it, or Delete to remove it.
Confirm.
en.body:
## Discontinue (stop)

- Takes effect **right away**, for the whole medication (every dose time).
- Upcoming doses leave the calendar and reminders stop.
- Past doses stay in the history and the reports.
- The medication moves to **Inactive medications**. Tap **Reactivate** there to turn it back on. Doses that passed while it was stopped don't come back.

## Delete

- The medication disappears from the medication list and the calendar, and its reminders stop.
- Doses already recorded stay in the history and the reports.
- This can't be undone. If you might need it again, use **Discontinue** instead.

## Good to know

- In the medication form, the same choices are under **Manage medication**.
- In the calendar, deleting a single dose asks **This dose only** or **This and all future doses**.
- On the web, open **Medications** and use the same **Discontinue** and **Delete** options on each card.

en.title: As-needed (PRN) medications
en.summary: Choose As needed under Repeat when you add the medication. It has no set times or reminders. Whoever gives a dose logs it, so the circle can see when it was last given.
steps: Tap New at the bottom of the screen, then Med. Type the Medication name and the Dosage.
Under Repeat, choose As needed.
Optionally fill in What is it for? (for example, pain or nausea), then tap Create Medication.
When you give a dose, tap Gave a dose on its card on Home.
Under Given, keep Now or tap an earlier time (such as 15 min ago), add a note if you like, and tap Log dose.
en.body:
## Good to know

- **No reminders and no alerts.** As-needed medications don't have a schedule.
- **Everyone sees it.** Logging a dose lets the circle know, and the card shows "Last given" with the time and who gave it.
- **Double-dose check.** If someone else logged the same medication in the last 30 minutes, the app asks before logging another.
- **Earlier doses.** You can log a dose from the last 48 hours, but never in the future.
- **History.** Tap **History** on the card to see every dose. You can remove a dose logged by mistake, and the circle is told.
- **Not part of adherence.** Reports list as-needed doses separately from the adherence rate.
- **Can't switch later.** A medication can't change between scheduled and as needed. Discontinue it and add it again.

CircleCare doesn't set limits on how often a dose can be logged. Follow the instructions from the doctor or pharmacist. The app is a tool, not a doctor.

On the web, the same **As needed** option is in the medication form.

en.title: Reminders for meals and daily routines
en.summary: Add meals, walks or other routines as a repeating Task assigned to the person who should do them. Keep medications for real medications.
steps: Tap New, then Task.
Enter a Title, such as Lunch.
Under Assigned to, choose the person who should be reminded.
Under Date & time, set the date and time, then under Repeat choose Daily or Days of the week.
Check Reminders: At the scheduled time is on, and you can add an earlier reminder.
Tap Create Task.
en.body:
## Why a task and not a medication

Adding a meal as a medication fills the medication list, the adherence numbers and the care summary with things that aren't medications. A doctor reading that summary would see "Lunch" next to real prescriptions. A repeating task reminds the same way and keeps medication records clean.

## Who gets the reminder

- The person in **Assigned to** gets it.
- If you leave it on **Anyone**, everyone in the circle who can edit gets it.
- Reminders are push notifications on phones. The web app doesn't send them.

## Good to know

- Tick the task off when it's done. The circle sees who did it.
- If you have [quiet hours](/help/quiet-hours/) set, task reminders during those hours are not sent.
- To change the routine later, edit the task. Changes apply to upcoming tasks only.

en.title: Add an appointment
en.summary: Tap New, choose Appointment, add a title, date, time and location, and save. Everyone in the circle sees it on the calendar.
steps: Tap New at the bottom of the screen, then Appointment.
Enter a Title, or tap a suggestion such as Doctor visit.
Add the Location and Details (optional).
Under Assigned to, choose who is taking them, or leave Anyone.
Set the Date & time. Then pick how long it lasts: 30 min, 1 hr or 2 hrs.
Set Reminders and tap Create Appointment.
en.body:
## Reminders

You can be reminded **At the scheduled time** and choose **Earlier reminders**: 24 hours, 1 hour, 30 minutes or 15 minutes before. The person in **Assigned to** gets them. With **Anyone**, everyone in the circle who can edit does.

## Good to know

- **Repeat** works the same as for tasks: daily, weekly, monthly and more.
- **Times are in the care recipient's time zone.**
- After the visit, open the appointment to add notes about what the doctor said.
- **Add by voice** is available on supported phones for Premium circles.
- On the web, open **Calendar** and add the appointment there.

## Limits

Reminders are push notifications on phones only. During [quiet hours](/help/quiet-hours/) they are not sent.

en.title: Share and assign tasks
en.summary: Add a task, assign it to someone or leave it for anyone, and the circle sees when it's done. Tasks can be one-time or repeating.
steps: Tap New, then Task.
Enter a Title, or tap a suggestion such as Grocery run.
Under Assigned to, choose a person, or leave Anyone.
Set a date and time if it has one, and a Repeat if it happens again.
Tap Create Task.
When it's done, open Care, then Tasks, and tap Done on it. Tap Undo if you marked the wrong one.
en.body:
## Where tasks live

Open **Care**, then **Tasks**. **Open** shows what still needs doing and **Completed** shows the last 30 days. You can sort by **Due date**, **Assignee** or **Created date**.

## Reminders

- A task with a time can send reminders: at the time and earlier (24 hours, 1 hour, 30 or 15 minutes before).
- The assigned person gets them. If the task is for **Anyone**, everyone in the circle who can edit does.
- People are also told when a task is assigned to them.

## Good to know

- **Completed tasks can't be edited**, but you can still open them and add notes. Delete is the only way to remove one.
- **Changes to a repeating task** apply to upcoming tasks. Completed and past ones stay as they were.
- People with view-only access can see tasks but not add or complete them.
- On the web, open **Tasks**.

en.title: Plan who is on care shifts
en.summary: With Premium, add blocks of time that need someone, such as nights or weekday mornings. Family can take open shifts, and everyone sees who is covering and what is still open.
steps: Open Care, then Calendar, and switch from Schedule to Shifts.
Tap Add shift.
Give it a Name, such as Night, and set when it Starts and Ends.
Choose if it Repeats, and set a Reminder for whoever is on it.
Under Who's covering?, choose Leave open or Me (the circle owner or a manager can pick anyone).
Tap Save shift. You can then tap Add the next shift to start where this one ends.
en.body:
## Taking and dropping shifts

- An **Open** shift has a **Take** button. For a repeating shift, choose **Just this one** or **This and every future one**.
- To give a shift back, open it and tap **Drop shift**. It becomes open again and everyone else in the circle is told.
- The circle owner or a manager can **Assign** a shift to someone, and can drop someone else's shift.
- There is no swap button. To swap, one person drops the shift and the other takes it.

## Notifications

On phones:

- When a new open shift is added, everyone else in the circle is told.
- When someone takes a shift, everyone else in the circle is told who is covering.
- When a shift is assigned to you, you are told.
- When someone drops a shift, everyone else in the circle is told.
- The circle owner and managers hear about shifts still open a day before they start.

Turn these on or off in Profile, Notifications, **Shifts**. The web app shows shifts but doesn't send notifications.

## Good to know

- **Premium only.** On a free circle, the owner sees a preview with **See Premium**.
- **If Premium ends**, shifts stay visible but become read-only until it is renewed.
- Shifts can run past midnight and last from 15 minutes to 24 hours.
- Times are in the care recipient's time zone.

en.title: See every visit and note for one doctor
en.summary: Choose the doctor when you add or edit an appointment. Then open that doctor under Doctors to see the next visit, past visits and their notes in one place.
steps: Add the doctor under Doctors in the Health tab, if they aren't there yet.
Add or edit an appointment and tap Doctor.
Choose the doctor, or tap Add a doctor, then save the appointment.
To see everything for that doctor, open Doctors and tap Visits & notes on their card.
Tap Add a note on any visit to write what was said.
en.body:
## What you see

**Visits & notes** shows the **Next visit**, then **Past visits**, newest first, with each visit's notes. Tap **Show earlier visits** to go further back. From a linked appointment, **See all visits** opens the same page.

## Good to know

- **Free for everyone.**
- **Past appointments are not linked for you.** CircleCare doesn't guess which doctor an old appointment was with. To add one, edit it and choose the doctor.
- **Repeating appointments** use one doctor for the whole series.
- **View-only members** can see visits and notes but can't add notes.
- The web app has the same doctor picker and **Visits & notes** page.

en.title: Write daily care notes
en.summary: Open Care, then Notes, write how the day went or pick a mood, and tap Post. Everyone in the circle sees the note with your name on it.
steps: Open your circle and tap “Care” at the bottom, then the “Notes” tab at the top.
Type in the box that says “How was the day?”.
Optionally pick a mood (“Great day”, “Good day”, “Okay” or “Tough day”) and one or more categories: “Meal”, “Medication”, “Visit” or “Incident”.
Tap “Post”.
To change or remove your note later, tap the pencil icon (“Edit note”) or the trash icon (“Delete note”) on it.
en.body:
Daily notes are a shared journal for the person you care for. Use them for how the day went, what they ate, a visit, or anything worth remembering.

## Good to know

- A note needs some text or a mood. You can post a mood on its own.
- Each note is filed under the day you post it, in the care recipient's time zone.
- Notes can be up to 2,000 characters.
- The week's moods show as a small strip above the list ("This week: ...").
- Everyone in the circle can read every note. Notes are not private to the author.

## Who can do what

- Anyone in the circle who can edit can write notes. A view-only member can read them but not post.
- Only the person who wrote a note can edit it.
- The author or the circle owner can delete a note. Deleting removes it for everyone.

## When people are told

Members who have the **Notes** notification group turned on get a push when someone adds a note. The push never shows what the note says. See [Quiet hours and turning notifications off](/help/quiet-hours/).

## On a computer

In the web companion, open **Notes** in the sidebar (under Care). The box is labelled **Add a note** and works the same way.

## Looking further back

The Notes list opens on the last two weeks, and **Show older notes** goes back as far as you like. See [Find older notes](/help/find-older-notes/).

en.title: Find older notes
en.summary: The Notes list opens on the last two weeks. Tap “Show older notes” at the bottom to go back further, as far as your notes go. There is no search for notes yet.
steps: Open “Care”, then “Notes”.
Scroll to the bottom of the list. On a phone, scrolling loads earlier days up to about three months back. Tap “Show older notes” to keep going back.
Keep tapping “Show older notes” until it says “No older notes”.
en.body:
There is no search for notes yet, but you can reach every note by going back through the list.

## How the list loads

- The Notes list opens on the last two weeks.
- On a phone, scrolling down loads earlier days, two weeks at a time, up to about three months back. On the web, tap **Show older notes** to do the same.
- Past that, each tap on **Show older notes** loads about three more months. There is no limit on how far back you can go.
- When there is nothing older, the list says **No older notes**.

Your notes are never deleted when they get old. Every note stays stored with its date, author and text.

## Need a copy of everything?

Use the data export. It is a file with your circle's records, including notes of every age.

- If you **own** the circle, the export includes every daily note and every visit or task note in it.
- If you are **a member** (not the owner), the export includes only the notes you wrote. Ask the circle owner to run it if you need everyone's notes.

See [Export your circle's data](/help/export-your-data/) for the steps.

## Need the last month for a doctor?

The care summary can include daily care notes from the last 30 days. See [Keep emergency info and share a care summary](/help/care-info-and-summary/).

## Before you update

This describes CircleCare 1.3.0. On earlier versions the list stops at about three months and the older notes are only in the data export.

en.title: Keep emergency info and share a care summary
en.summary: Store contacts, doctors, insurance, allergies and conditions once in Emergency info, and anyone in the circle can see them. Tap Share to send a care summary PDF to a doctor, hospital or relative.
steps: Open your circle and tap “Health” at the bottom. It opens on “Emergency info”. From Home you can also tap the “Health” shortcut.
Tap the + next to a section, such as “Critical information”, or a row that says “Tap to add”, to fill in medical information, doctors, emergency contacts or insurance.
To share, tap the share icon at the top right. The “Share care summary” sheet opens.
Choose whether to “Include visit notes” and “Include daily care notes”.
Tap “Share” and pick how to send the PDF.
en.body:
Emergency info is the one place for the facts someone may need fast, at the pharmacy, the ER, or on the phone with a nurse.

## Where to find it

The app names this area in a few places. On a phone it is the **Health** tab, then **Emergency**, and the screen is titled **Emergency info**. On the web it is **Emergency Info** in the sidebar, under Health.

## What you can store

- **Medical information**: blood type, medication allergies, other allergies, and conditions.
- **Doctors**: a primary doctor and specialists.
- **Emergency contacts**.
- **Insurance**.
- **Current medications** come from the medications you already added. You don't type them twice.

It is stored once for the circle and everyone in the circle can see it. Members who can edit can change it; view-only members can read it.

## What the care summary PDF includes

- The care recipient's name, date of birth, conditions and allergies
- Emergency contacts
- Current medications, plus medications stopped in the last 30 days
- Doctors
- Insurance
- Optional: visit notes and daily care notes from the last 30 days, if you turn those switches on

It does **not** include vitals or medication adherence. Those are in the adherence report. See [Export your circle's data](/help/export-your-data/).

## Who can share it

Anyone in the circle can create and share the summary, including view-only members. Before it is shared, the app reminds you that it contains sensitive health information. Only share it with people you trust.

## On a computer

Open **Emergency Info** and click **Share**. The summary opens in your browser's print window, where you can print it or save it as a PDF.

CircleCare stores and shares the information you enter. It does not review it or give medical advice.

en.title: Store documents and photos
en.summary: Upload insurance cards, records and other papers as photos or PDFs under Health, then Documents, so anyone in the circle can open them. Each file can be up to 10MB, and a circle has 200MB on the free plan or 1GB on Premium.
steps: Open your circle and tap “Health”, then the “Documents” tab.
Tap the add button at the top right (or a “Start here” suggestion).
Tap “Choose photo” or “Choose file (PDF)”.
Give it a “Label”, pick a “Category” and add a “Note” if it helps.
Tap “Upload”.
en.body:
Keep the papers people ask for in one place: insurance cards (front and back), an advance directive, the pharmacy's medication list, recent lab results.

## Files you can add

- Photos: JPG, PNG and HEIC (iPhone photos)
- PDF files
- Up to 10MB per file

Categories: **Medical records**, **Insurance**, **Legal**, **Prescriptions** and **Other**. You can filter the list by category.

## Storage

Storage is shared by the whole circle, and the amount depends on the **circle owner's** plan:

- Free: 200MB per circle
- Premium: 1GB per circle

The Documents screen shows how much is used. When it is full, deleting files frees space. Only the circle owner can upgrade for more. See [What is free and what Premium adds](/help/free-and-premium/).

## Who can do what

- Anyone in the circle can open and view documents.
- Members who can edit can upload. A view-only member cannot add, rename or remove documents.
- Only the person who uploaded a document, or the circle owner, can rename or delete it.

## Deleting is permanent

When you delete a document, the file is removed for everyone and cannot be recovered. If you might need it later, save a copy first with **Share**.

## On a computer

Open **Documents** in the web sidebar and click **Upload document**. The web accepts JPG, PNG, HEIC or PDF, up to 10MB.

en.title: Track blood pressure, heart rate, glucose and weight
en.summary: Log blood pressure, heart rate, glucose and weight by hand, and everyone in the circle sees each reading and who logged it. CircleCare does not sync with Apple Health or other devices.
steps: From your circle's Home, tap “Vitals”.
Choose the type of reading at the top, such as “Blood pressure”.
Tap the add button (+) at the top right.
Enter the numbers. Change the date and time if the reading was earlier, and add notes if you like.
Tap “Save reading”.
en.body:
Vitals help the circle notice a trend before the next appointment.

## What you can track

- **Blood pressure** (mmHg, systolic and diastolic)
- **Heart rate** (bpm)
- **Glucose** (mg/dL or mmol/L)
- **Weight** (lbs or kg)

The web companion and the newest version of the app also have **Temperature** and **Blood oxygen**. If you don't see them on your phone, update CircleCare.

## How readings are shared

Every reading is visible to everyone in the circle, with the name of the person who logged it ("Logged by ..."). The screen shows the latest reading, the average, the lowest and highest, and a trend chart over a week, month, six months or year.

Members who can edit can add, change and delete readings. View-only members can see them.

## Units

Choose your units in Profile, under **Health units**. Readings are converted, so you and your sister can each see your own units.

## What vitals don't do

- Readings are entered by hand. CircleCare does not connect to Apple Health, Google Health Connect, blood pressure cuffs or glucose meters.
- CircleCare does not interpret readings or tell you what they mean. Talk to a doctor or nurse about any reading that worries you.

## Share readings with a doctor

The adherence report (Premium) can include a summary of vitals for the period you pick. See [Export your circle's data](/help/export-your-data/). The care summary PDF does not include vitals.

## On a computer

Open **Vitals** in the web sidebar.

en.title: Export your circle's data
en.summary: In Profile, under Your data, tap Download my data to get a JSON file of what CircleCare stores. Circle owners get the whole circle's records; members get their own.
steps: Open Profile. On a phone, go back to your list of circles and tap the person icon at the top.
Scroll to “Your data”.
Tap “Download my data”.
On a phone, choose where to save or send the file. On the web, the file downloads to your computer.
en.body:
There are three different exports in CircleCare. They do different jobs.

## 1. Your data (the full export)

A file named circlecare-export.json. JSON is a data format, not a printable report. It is best for keeping a complete copy or moving your records to another tool.

**If you own a circle**, it includes for that circle:

- The care recipient's details and the member list
- Emergency info
- Medications and every recorded dose (taken, late, skipped), plus as-needed doses
- Appointments and tasks
- Vitals
- Daily care notes and visit or task notes, of every age
- The list of documents (name, category, type, size, date). The files themselves are not inside; download those from Documents.

**If you are a member** of someone else's circle, it includes your membership and the records you created there: events you added, doses you recorded and notes you wrote.

Archived circles are not included. You can run the export up to 5 times a day. Anyone can export their own data; you don't need Premium.

## 2. Care summary (PDF)

A short document for a doctor or hospital: the care recipient, conditions, allergies, emergency contacts, medications, doctors and insurance, with optional notes from the last 30 days. Anyone in the circle can share it. See [Keep emergency info and share a care summary](/help/care-info-and-summary/).

## 3. Medication history report (PDF, Premium)

A printable report of what was taken, taken late, skipped or not marked over a period you pick. See [Share a medication history report](/help/medication-history-report/).

en.title: Share a medication history report
en.summary: Open Care, then Meds, tap History and then Export report. Pick a period from the last 7 days to all time, and CircleCare makes a PDF of the doses taken, taken late, skipped or not marked. It needs a Premium circle.
steps: Open “Care”, then “Meds”, and tap “History”. On the web, open “Medications” and choose “History”.
On the adherence card at the top, tap “Export report”.
Choose a period: “Last 7 days”, “Last 14 days”, “Last 30 days”, “Last 60 days”, “Last 90 days” or “All time”.
Wait while it says “Generating PDF...”, then choose where to save or send the PDF. On the web, the report opens in your browser's print window, where you can print it or save it as a PDF.
en.body:
The report is a PDF for a doctor, a pharmacist or the rest of the family. It covers every scheduled dose in the period, up to yesterday. Today isn't counted yet, because some of today's doses may still be ahead.

## What it counts

Each scheduled dose is one of:

- **Taken**: marked as taken within 30 minutes of its time.
- **Taken late**: marked as taken 30 minutes or more after its time.
- **Skipped**: someone marked it as skipped.
- **Not marked**: no one confirmed it in the app. It may or may not have been taken.

The adherence rate is the doses taken (on time or late) out of the doses scheduled. The report shows:

- **Summary**: the rate, the counts above and whether the second half of the period went better or worse than the first.
- **By medication**: the dosage, taken, not marked, skipped and rate for each medication.
- **By day**: one square per day (the last 30 days of the period) and a list of the days with a skipped or unmarked dose.
- **Time of day**: the same counts for each dose time.

As-needed medications are listed in their own section (doses given and by whom) and don't count toward the rate. A medication that was stopped counts only the doses that were due before it was stopped.

## Vitals summary

A report made on the web also includes a summary of the vitals recorded in the same period, if there are any: for each type, the latest reading, the average, the lowest and the highest. Reports made in the phone app don't include vitals yet. To look at readings, see [Track blood pressure, heart rate, glucose and weight](/help/vitals/).

## Notes and limits

- It needs a **Premium circle**: the circle owner's plan. In a free circle, the owner sees the upgrade options when tapping Export report, and other members see that the owner needs Premium. See [What is free and what Premium adds](/help/free-and-premium/).
- The adherence card and its Export report button appear once the circle has had scheduled doses in the last 30 days.
- “All time” starts from the first dose anyone marked in the circle.
- Anyone in the circle can make the report, including members with view-only access.
- The PDF shows the care recipient's name, date of birth and medication history. Share it only with people who should see it.
- For a one-page summary of conditions, allergies, medications and doctors, use the care summary instead. See [Keep emergency info and share a care summary](/help/care-info-and-summary/). For a full copy of everything, see [Export your circle's data](/help/export-your-data/).

en.title: Log a fall or incident that already happened
en.summary: Write a daily note, set its Date to the day it happened, and pick the Incident category. The note is filed under that day, even if it was weeks or years ago.
steps: Open “Care”, then “Notes”.
Write what happened in the box that says “How was the day?”.
Tap the “Date” row under the text (it says “Today”), pick the day it happened, then tap “Confirm”. Future dates can't be picked.
Pick the “Incident” category.
Tap “Post”. The note appears under its own day.
en.body:
Falls, a bad reaction, a trip to the ER: these matter months later, when a doctor asks "when did that happen?". Now you can log them on the right date, even if you only remember to write it down later.

## Example: a fall from a few weeks ago

Your mother fell on May 5 and you are logging it today. Write "Fell in the bathroom, bruised left hip, no ER visit", set **Date** to May 5, pick **Incident** and tap **Post**. The note is filed under May 5, not today.

## Good to know

- The date can be today or any earlier day. There is no limit on how far back.
- To go back to today before posting, tap **Reset to today**.
- The author can change a note's date later by editing it.
- The circle gets the usual note notification, and it names the day the note is for. It never shows what the note says.
- To see older days in the list, scroll to the bottom and tap **Show older notes**.

## On a computer

The web companion has the same **Date** row in the note box on the **Notes** page.

CircleCare keeps a record of what you write. It does not assess injuries or give medical advice. If someone has fallen and may be hurt, call a doctor or emergency services.

en.title: Not getting notifications
en.summary: Most often the phone's notification permission for CircleCare is off, the phone is signed in to a different account, quiet hours are on, or that type of notification is turned off in Profile. Go through the checks below in order.
steps: Check the phone: in your phone's Settings, find CircleCare and make sure notifications are allowed. If they're blocked, Profile in the app shows “Notifications are blocked” with an “Open Settings” button.
Check the account: open Profile on that phone and confirm it shows your name and email.
Check the notification groups: in Profile, under “Notifications”, make sure the groups you want are on.
Check quiet hours: in Profile, under “Quiet hours”, see if “Enable quiet hours” is on and what times it covers.
Check who the reminder is for: dose reminders and task reminders go to specific people, not always to everyone.
en.body:
Notifications depend on the phone, the account and a few settings. Here's what each check means.

## 1. The phone allows CircleCare notifications

If notifications were turned off for CircleCare (or never allowed), the phone silently drops them. In the app, Profile shows **Notifications are off** or **Notifications are blocked** with a button to turn them on. A Focus or Do Not Disturb mode on the phone can also hide them.

## 2. The phone is signed in to the right account

A phone gets notifications for **one CircleCare account at a time**: the one most recently signed in on it. If a shared family phone or tablet was last signed in as someone else, it gets that person's notifications, not yours. Sign in with your own account on your own phone and open the app once. Signing out doesn't stop a phone's notifications; signing in with another account does.

## 3. Notification groups

In Profile, under **Notifications**, there is one switch per group, such as **Medications**, **Tasks & appointments**, **Notes** and **Daily update & tips**. They apply to your account in every circle. If a group shows **Some turned off**, part of it is off.

## 4. Quiet hours

During your quiet hours, some notifications are held until the end and some are skipped. See [Quiet hours and turning notifications off](/help/quiet-hours/).

## 5. Who each reminder goes to

- **Dose reminders** go to one person: the member the owner chose for **Medication reminders** (this covers every medication in the circle), or the care recipient if they are in the circle, or otherwise the circle owner. That person gets the reminders before and at the dose time, and the alert 15 minutes later. If the chosen member has view-only access, these go to the care recipient or the owner instead. Later missed-dose alerts reach more people in the circle. Reminder times are set on each medication. See [How reminders and missed-dose alerts work](/help/reminders-and-alerts/).
- **Task reminders** go to the person the task is assigned to. A task set to "Anyone" reminds everyone in the circle who can act on it.
- If your seat in a circle is **view-only**, you don't get that circle's notifications. See [Owners, caregivers, care recipients and view-only](/help/roles-and-permissions/).

## 6. The web doesn't send notifications

The web companion lets you change your notification settings, but it does not deliver notifications. Install the app on your phone to receive them. See [Use CircleCare on a computer](/help/use-on-a-computer/).

Still stuck? Contact us from the Help page and tell us which notification you expected and roughly when.

en.title: Quiet hours and turning notifications off
en.summary: Quiet hours hold most notifications until your quiet time ends, so you catch up in the morning. Reminders that only make sense ahead of time, like “in 15 minutes”, are skipped. You can also turn whole groups of notifications off in Profile.
steps: Open Profile. On a phone, go back to your list of circles and tap the person icon at the top.
Under “Quiet hours”, turn on “Enable quiet hours”.
Set “Start” and “End”.
Tap “Save quiet hours”. Turning quiet hours off saves right away. On the web, changes save on their own.
To turn off a type of notification, use the switches under “Notifications”.
en.body:
Quiet hours are yours alone. They follow your time zone and don't change anything for other people in the circle. New accounts start with quiet hours off.

## What happens during quiet hours

**Held and delivered when quiet hours end:**

- Alerts that a dose is late or wasn't marked. If someone marks the dose during the night, the alert is dropped, and several alerts about the same dose arrive as one.
- Updates from the circle: a dose taken or skipped, a new note, a task assigned to you, a new appointment, a task completed, refill alerts.
- Shift alerts that are still useful later: a shift was dropped, shifts were reopened because someone left the circle, and, for the owner and managers, a shift still open a day before it starts.

**Skipped, not delivered later:**

- Reminders before or at a dose's time ("in 1 hour", "in 15 minutes", "Time for medication"). Sending them in the morning would be wrong. If the dose still isn't marked about 15 minutes after its time, the follow-up alert is held for the morning instead.
- Task and appointment reminders that say how soon something is due.
- Shift alerts for a new open shift, a shift someone took or assigned to you, shift reminders and time changes.

When you add a medication and its time falls inside your own quiet hours, the app warns you that no reminder will be sent then. It only checks your quiet hours, and only when the reminder goes to you. If a medication is taken at night, shorten or move quiet hours so the reminder can come through.

If quiet hours cover almost the whole day, the app warns you that notifications will be held until the end time.

## Turn off types of notifications

In Profile, under **Notifications**:

- **Medications**: doses taken, skipped or not marked. Turning this off means you won't be told when a dose isn't marked, so the app asks you to confirm.
- **Tasks & appointments**: when something's assigned to you and before it's due.
- **Notes**: when someone adds a note.
- **Daily update & tips**: your daily update and helpful nudges.
- **Shifts**: new open shifts, shift reminders and changes to your shifts. See [Plan who is on care shifts](/help/care-shifts/).

These switches apply to your account in every circle. The reminder times for each medication are set on the medication itself. See [How reminders and missed-dose alerts work](/help/reminders-and-alerts/).

Notifications only arrive on a phone with the app installed. See [Not getting notifications](/help/notifications-not-arriving/).

en.title: What is free and what Premium adds
en.summary: The free plan has no time limit and includes 1 care circle with you plus 1 caregiver, and unlimited medications and reminders. Premium adds up to 5 circles, unlimited caregivers, more document storage and the care assistant.
en.body:
## Free plan

- 1 care circle that you own
- You plus 1 caregiver in that circle (the care recipient does not count)
- Unlimited medications and reminders. Reminders are never behind a paywall.
- Calendar, appointments, tasks, notes, vitals, emergency info and the activity history
- 200MB of documents and photos per circle

## Premium

- Up to 5 care circles that you own
- Unlimited caregivers in each circle
- 1GB of documents and photos per circle
- The care assistant ("Assistant" in the app)
- Care shifts, to plan who is on call (see [Plan who is on care shifts](/help/care-shifts/))
- Managers, caregivers you choose to help invite and remove people (see [Owners, caregivers, care recipients and view-only](/help/roles-and-permissions/))
- Adherence reports and importing appointments from your calendar
- Adding by voice, in the phone app on supported phones
- The weekly care summary email

## Who pays

Only the circle owner pays. Premium applies to the circles that person owns, so everyone in those circles gets the Premium features there. Joining someone else's circle is always free.

## Price and free trial

Prices are set in the App Store and Google Play and vary by country. The app shows your price before you buy. The yearly plan can include a 7-day free trial if your store account is eligible. In the phone app, tap **Upgrade to Premium** at the top of Profile. You can also upgrade on the web at my.circlecare.app under "Profile".

## If Premium ends

Nothing is deleted.

- On a circle with more caregivers than the free plan allows, the caregiver who joined first keeps editing and the others become view-only.
- Managers go back to being caregivers. If you subscribe again, you choose managers again.
- Existing shifts stay visible but become read-only.
- If you own more than one circle, the app asks you to choose one to keep with free access ("Choose circle"). The others become read-only for everyone until you subscribe again. You can make this choice only once.
- When you subscribe again, everything goes back to normal.

See [Cancel, restore or change your subscription](/help/cancel-or-restore/).

en.title: Care for more than one person
en.summary: Each person you care for gets their own circle. The free plan lets you own 1 circle. To own more, up to 5, you need Premium. Joining circles that other people own is always free.
steps: Go to your list of circles. From inside a circle, tap the back arrow at the top left.
Tap the "+" button ("Start a care circle").
If you are on the free plan and already own a circle, the app shows the Premium plans. Choose a plan to continue.
Fill in the new person's details and tap "Create circle".
en.body:
## Free ways to care for two people

- **Let someone else own the second circle.** For example, your sister creates Dad's circle and invites you. You can be a member of any number of circles for free.
- A circle you create for yourself ("Myself") counts as one of your own circles.

## Good to know

- Premium allows up to 5 circles that you own. If you need more, write to support@circlecare.app.
- If you delete a circle, it no longer counts toward your limit.
- Each circle is separate. Medications, notes and members do not mix between circles.
- Switch circles from your list of circles in the app, or with "All circles" on the website.
- If your Premium ends while you own several circles, you choose one to keep with free access and the others become read-only. Nothing is deleted. See [What is free and what Premium adds](/help/free-and-premium/).

en.title: Cancel, restore or change your subscription
en.summary: Cancel where you subscribed: in the App Store or Google Play if you bought it on your phone, or with "Manage subscription" in your web Profile if you bought it on the web. You keep Premium until the end of the period you paid for.
steps: In the app, open "Profile" (the person icon on your list of circles).
Under "Subscription", tap "Manage". This opens the subscription page of the store where you subscribed.
Cancel or change your plan there.
If your subscription is not shown, tap "Restore purchases" under "Account" in Profile.
en.body:
## Cancel from your phone settings

- **iPhone:** Settings, tap your name, then Subscriptions.
- **Android:** Google Play Store, Payments & subscriptions, then Subscriptions.

## If you subscribed on the web

Go to my.circlecare.app, open "Profile" and choose "Manage subscription". If you subscribed on your phone, the website tells you to cancel in the App Store or Google Play instead.

## Restore purchases

Use "Restore purchases" when you get a new phone, reinstall the app, or Premium does not show up. Sign in to the same CircleCare account first. The app tells you if no purchases were found. A subscription bought on the web is linked to your account and does not need restoring.

## After you cancel

You keep Premium until the end of the period you already paid for. After that, nothing is deleted. Extra caregivers become view-only, and if you own more than one circle you choose one to keep with free access. Subscribe again at any time to get everything back. See [What is free and what Premium adds](/help/free-and-premium/).

## Good to know

- There are no contracts or cancellation fees. You can cancel during a free trial.
- Deleting your account does not cancel a subscription. Cancel it first. See [Delete your account](/help/delete-account/).
- If your Premium has ended or a payment did not go through, Profile shows "Manage existing subscription" so you can still reach the store page.

en.title: Delete your account
en.summary: Open "Profile", tap "Delete account" and confirm. This permanently deletes your account and every care circle you own. It cannot be undone.
steps: If you have Premium, cancel your subscription first in the App Store, Google Play or your web Profile. Deleting your account does not cancel it.
Optional: tap "Download my data" in Profile to keep a copy of your information.
Open "Profile" and scroll to "Account".
Tap "Delete account".
Read the message and tap "Delete my account" to confirm.
en.body:
## What gets deleted

- Your account and your sign-in.
- **Every circle you own**, with all its medications, appointments, tasks, notes, vitals, documents and emergency info. Everyone else in those circles loses access and is notified.
- Invitations you sent that were not accepted yet.

## What stays

Circles that someone else owns are not deleted. You are removed from them. What you added there, such as notes, activity, documents and photos, stays in the circle, but your name is removed from it.

## If you cannot open the app

Use the [account deletion page](https://circlecare.app/account-deletion). Enter your account email and we send you a verification code. The code works for 15 minutes. Enter it to confirm the deletion.

## Before you delete

- If you want the circle to continue for your family, talk to them first. Ownership cannot be handed to someone else.
- To leave just one circle instead of deleting your account, open that circle and tap "Leave circle".
- On a computer, you can also delete your account from "Profile" at my.circlecare.app with "Delete my account".
- Some data may stay in backups for up to 30 days before it is gone. See our [privacy policy](https://circlecare.app/privacy).

en.title: Privacy, security and HIPAA
en.summary: Only people in your circle can see your circle's information. Data is encrypted in transit and at rest and stored in the United States. There are no ads and we never sell your data. CircleCare is not HIPAA compliant and does not sign BAAs.
en.body:
## Who can see your information

Only people who joined your circle. What each person can do depends on their role, and these rules are checked on our servers, not only in the app. See [Owners, caregivers, care recipients and view-only](/help/roles-and-permissions/).

The circle owner, or a manager (for caregivers only), can remove someone at any time: in "Care team", tap the person, then "Remove from circle". They lose access to the circle.

## How it is protected

- Data is encrypted in transit (HTTPS/TLS) and at rest.
- Data is stored in the United States.

## Ads and selling data

There are no ads in CircleCare. We do not sell your information and do not share your health data with advertisers.

## HIPAA

CircleCare is a consumer app for families. It is **not HIPAA compliant** and we do not sign Business Associate Agreements (BAAs), on any plan. If your organization needs HIPAA compliance, CircleCare is not the right tool for that.

## Usage analytics

In Profile, under "Privacy", the "Usage analytics" switch lets you choose whether usage data and crash reports linked to your account are shared to help us improve CircleCare. They never include your readings, medication names or notes. With it off, we still collect anonymous, session-only data that is never linked to you. On the web, the same choice is "Share usage data" in Profile.

## Signing in

- There is no two-step (two-factor) sign-in.
- On your phone you can turn on Face ID, Touch ID or fingerprint sign-in under "Security" in Profile (it shows when your phone has one set up). Your fingerprint or face never leaves your phone.
- Use a strong password, or sign in with Google or Apple.

## Your data, your choice

- Download a copy of your information with "Download my data" in Profile. See [Export your circle's data](/help/export-your-data/).
- Delete your account at any time. See [Delete your account](/help/delete-account/).

Read the full [privacy policy](https://circlecare.app/privacy). In the app, "Privacy Policy" and "Terms of Service" are in Profile, under "Support".

es.title: Crea tu primer círculo de cuidado
es.summary: Un círculo de cuidado es un espacio privado para una persona que cuidas. Crea tu cuenta, elige a quién cuidas, escribe su nombre y toca "Crear círculo". Toma como un minuto y es gratis.
steps: Descarga CircleCare en tu iPhone o celular Android y toca "Comenzar" para crear tu cuenta.
En "¿A quién estás cuidando?", elige "A un padre o madre", "A mi pareja", "A mi hijo/a", "A mí" o "A otra persona".
Escribe su nombre o cómo le llamas, por ejemplo Mamá o Abuelo. La fecha de nacimiento es opcional.
Toca "Crear círculo".
Elige un primer paso: agregar un medicamento, una cita, invitar a alguien o agregar información de emergencia. También puedes tocar "Omitir por ahora" y volver después.
es.body:
## ¿Alguien te invitó?

Si un familiar ya creó un círculo y te invitó, **no crees uno nuevo**. Abre el enlace de invitación que te llegó por correo, o toca "¿Tienes un código de invitación?". Si tienes una invitación esperando, la pantalla "Crear círculo" muestra un aviso que dice "Tienes 1 invitación pendiente". Toca "Revisar invitación" para unirte. Consulta [Únete a un círculo al que te invitaron](/help/join-a-circle/).

## Bueno saber

- Cada círculo es para una sola persona. Si cuidas a tu mamá y a tu papá, consulta [Cuidar a más de una persona](/help/second-circle/).
- Si eliges "A mí", el círculo es para tu propio cuidado. Eres a la vez propietario y receptor de cuidado, y puedes invitar a tu familia para que te ayude.
- Después de crear tu primer círculo, la app puede mostrarte una vez los planes Premium. Puedes tocar "Continuar con plan gratuito" y seguir usando CircleCare gratis.
- También puedes crear un círculo desde la computadora en my.circlecare.app: haz clic en "Crear círculo" en la lista de tus círculos. Consulta [Usa CircleCare en la computadora](/help/use-on-a-computer/).

## Qué sigue

1. [Agrega un medicamento y sus recordatorios](/help/add-a-medication/).
2. [Invita a tu familia y a otros cuidadores](/help/invite-family/).
3. [Guarda la información de emergencia y comparte un resumen de cuidado](/help/care-info-and-summary/).

es.title: Invita a tu familia y a otros cuidadores
es.summary: El propietario del círculo invita a otras personas por correo desde la pantalla de Inicio del círculo. Reciben un correo con un enlace y un código de 6 caracteres, y unirse siempre es gratis para ellos.
steps: Abre el círculo y quédate en la pestaña "Inicio".
Baja hasta "Equipo de cuidado" y toca "Agregar familiar".
En "¿A quién estás invitando?", elige "Cuidador familiar" o "Receptor de cuidado".
Escribe su correo electrónico y toca "Enviar invitación".
Si quieres, toca "Compartir enlace de invitación" o "Copiar enlace" para mandarlo por mensaje o chat, y así pueda unirse de inmediato.
es.body:
## Qué recibe la persona invitada

CircleCare le manda un correo con un enlace y un código de invitación. Si abre el enlace en un celular que tiene CircleCare, se abre la app. Si no tiene la app, el enlace se abre en su navegador y puede unirse desde ahí. Necesita una cuenta gratuita. Consulta [Únete a un círculo al que te invitaron](/help/join-a-circle/).

## Cuidador o receptor de cuidado

- **Cuidador familiar** es para hermanos, pareja, amigos o cuidadores pagados que ayudan con el cuidado.
- **Receptor de cuidado** es la persona a la que cuidan. Recibe una versión más sencilla de la app, enfocada en los recordatorios de medicamentos, y puede confirmar cuando ya tomó una dosis. Un círculo solo puede tener un receptor de cuidado. El círculo funciona aunque esa persona no tenga cuenta.

## Límites del plan gratuito

- Un círculo gratuito te incluye a ti y a 1 cuidador. Una invitación pendiente ocupa ese lugar hasta que la aceptan, la cancelas o vence.
- Si el lugar está ocupado por una invitación pendiente, la app muestra "Tu invitación ya está en uso". Cancela esa invitación para liberar el lugar, o mejora tu plan.
- Invitar al receptor de cuidado nunca tiene límite. No cuenta dentro del límite de cuidadores.
- Con Premium puedes invitar a todos los cuidadores que necesites. Consulta [Qué es gratis y qué agrega Premium](/help/free-and-premium/).

## Invitaciones pendientes

Las invitaciones duran 7 días. En "Equipo de cuidado", la sección "Invitaciones pendientes" muestra cada una y cuándo vence. Cuando una invitación ya venció, toca "Reenviar" para mandarla otra vez por 7 días más. Para retirar una, toca la X junto a ella.

## Bueno saber

- Solo el propietario del círculo y los gestores pueden invitar. Los demás cuidadores no pueden enviar invitaciones. Consulta [Propietario, cuidadores, receptor de cuidado y solo lectura](/help/roles-and-permissions/).
- Desde la computadora, en my.circlecare.app, abre el círculo, entra a "Miembros" y luego a "Invitar miembro".

es.title: Únete a un círculo al que te invitaron
es.summary: Abre el enlace de invitación que te llegó por correo y sigue los pasos para crear una cuenta gratuita. Te unes al círculo en ese momento. Unirte al círculo de otra persona siempre es gratis.
steps: Busca el correo de invitación de CircleCare. Si no lo ves, revisa la carpeta de spam o promociones.
Toca el enlace del correo. Si tienes CircleCare en tu celular, se abre la app. Si no, la invitación se abre en tu navegador.
En la app se abre la pantalla "Ingresa tu código de invitación" con tu código ya escrito. Escribe el correo al que te llegó la invitación y toca "Continuar".
Revisa quién te invitó y toca "Continuar para crear cuenta" en la app, o "Crea una cuenta para unirte" en el navegador.
Crea tu cuenta. En la app, toca "Crear cuenta y unirme".
Si ya tienes cuenta, elige "Iniciar sesión" (o "Ya tengo una cuenta" en el navegador). Te unes al círculo en cuanto inicias sesión.
es.body:
## Si solo tienes el código

El correo de invitación también trae un código de 6 caracteres. Abre la app y toca "¿Tienes un código de invitación?" y luego "Ingresar código". Escribe el correo al que te llegó la invitación y el código. Desde la computadora, en my.circlecare.app, elige "Unirte con un código de invitación".

## Si la app te pide crear un círculo

Después de registrarte, la app puede mostrarte la pantalla "Crear círculo". Si alguien te invitó, **no necesitas tu propio círculo**.

- Busca arriba el aviso "Tienes 1 invitación pendiente", toca "Revisar invitación" y luego "Aceptar".
- O toca "¿Tienes un código de invitación?" al final de la pantalla y escribe tu código.

## Si ya creaste un círculo por error

Tu invitación sigue funcionando. En tu lista de círculos, toca la tarjeta de invitaciones ("Toca para revisar y unirte a círculos") y acéptala. Desde la computadora, entra a "Tus invitaciones".

Después puedes eliminar el círculo que sobra: ábrelo, ve a "Administrar" y toca "Eliminar círculo". Un círculo eliminado ya no cuenta como tu círculo gratuito, así que más adelante puedes crear el tuyo.

## Si la invitación no funciona

- Las invitaciones duran 7 días. Si la tuya venció, pídele a quien te invitó que toque "Reenviar" o te mande una nueva.
- Para unirte desde la lista de invitaciones pendientes, inicia sesión con el mismo correo al que te llegó la invitación. Si usas otro correo (por ejemplo "Ocultar mi correo" de Apple), usa el enlace o el código.

## Bueno saber

- Que te inviten nunca cuesta nada, ni en el plan gratuito ni en Premium. Solo el propietario del círculo puede pagar Premium.
- Puedes estar en varios círculos, por ejemplo el de tu mamá y el de tu papá.

es.title: Propietario, cuidadores, receptor de cuidado y solo lectura
es.summary: Cada círculo tiene un propietario, que es quien lo creó. Los cuidadores pueden ver y actualizar la información de cuidado. Un gestor es un cuidador que además puede invitar y quitar personas. El receptor de cuidado recibe recordatorios y confirma sus dosis. Solo lectura significa que puedes ver todo pero no hacer cambios.
es.body:
## Propietario del círculo

Es la persona que creó el círculo. El propietario puede invitar personas, cancelar o reenviar invitaciones y quitar miembros, y es el único que puede:

- cambiar los datos del círculo (**Editar círculo**)
- eliminar el círculo (**Eliminar círculo**)
- elegir quién recibe los recordatorios de medicamentos
- dar o quitar el rol de gestor
- pagar Premium para el círculo

## Gestor

Un gestor es un cuidador a quien el propietario eligió para ayudar a administrar el círculo. Los gestores pueden:

- invitar personas, y reenviar o cancelar cualquier invitación pendiente
- ver las invitaciones pendientes
- quitar cuidadores del círculo (nunca al propietario ni a otro gestor)
- poner a otra persona en un turno de cuidado o quitarla de uno (consulta [Organiza quién cubre cada turno de cuidado](/help/care-shifts/))

Los gestores no pueden cambiar los datos del círculo, eliminar el círculo, elegir quién recibe los recordatorios de medicamentos, manejar la facturación ni dar el rol de gestor a otras personas. Un círculo puede tener más de un gestor.

Para dar el rol de gestor a alguien, el propietario abre el círculo, toca a la persona en la lista de miembros (en la web, usa el menú de su fila en **Miembros**) y elige **Dar rol de gestor**. Para deshacerlo, elige **Quitar rol de gestor**. La persona sigue en el círculo como cuidador.

Conviene saber:

- Los gestores son una función Premium. Depende del plan del propietario, así que solo el propietario necesita Premium. Si se termina el Premium del propietario, todos los gestores vuelven a ser cuidadores. Las invitaciones que ya enviaron siguen vigentes. Si el propietario se suscribe de nuevo, tiene que elegir otra vez a los gestores.
- El receptor de cuidado y los miembros de solo lectura no pueden ser gestores.
- Los límites de lugares siguen siendo los del propietario. En el plan gratuito el círculo tiene espacio para el propietario y 1 cuidador, sin importar quién envíe la invitación.
- Un gestor ve las herramientas de gestor en CircleCare 1.3.0 o posterior, y en el sitio web. Las versiones anteriores de la app muestran a un gestor como un cuidador normal.

## Cuidador

Familiares y personas que ayudan. Al invitar a alguien, es la opción **Cuidador familiar**. Los cuidadores pueden ver y actualizar la información de cuidado: medicamentos, dosis, citas, tareas, notas, signos vitales, documentos e información de emergencia. Un cuidador puede salir del círculo cuando quiera con **Salir del círculo**, al final de Inicio.

## Receptor de cuidado

Es la persona a la que cuidan. Si se une con su propia cuenta, recibe recordatorios de medicamentos y puede confirmar cuando tomó una dosis; la familia recibe el aviso. Un círculo tiene como máximo un receptor de cuidado, y no cuenta dentro del límite de cuidadores del plan gratuito. En un círculo que creas para ti ("A mí"), eres a la vez propietario y receptor de cuidado.

## Solo lectura

Una persona con acceso de solo lectura puede ver todo en el círculo, pero no puede hacer cambios. Ve el aviso "Tienes acceso de solo lectura" y el botón **Nuevo** aparece atenuado. Esto pasa cuando:

- un círculo gratuito tiene más cuidadores de los que permite el plan gratuito, por ejemplo cuando se termina el Premium del propietario. El cuidador que se unió primero sigue editando y los demás quedan en solo lectura.
- se terminó el Premium del propietario y tenía más de un círculo. Los círculos que no conservó quedan en solo lectura para todos.

Cuando el propietario vuelve a suscribirse, todos pueden editar otra vez. No se borra nada. Consulta [Qué es gratis y qué agrega Premium](/help/free-and-premium/).

## Dónde se aplican estas reglas

Estas reglas se revisan en los servidores de CircleCare, no solo en la app. Nadie sin permiso puede saltárselas usando otro dispositivo o el sitio web.

es.title: Usa CircleCare en la computadora
es.summary: Entra a my.circlecare.app desde cualquier navegador e inicia sesión con la misma cuenta de tu celular. Verás los mismos círculos y la misma información. Los recordatorios y alertas solo llegan a la app del celular.
steps: Abre un navegador en tu computadora y entra a my.circlecare.app.
Inicia sesión con el mismo correo, o la misma cuenta de Google o Apple, que usas en la app del celular.
Se abre tu círculo. Si tienes más de uno, elígelo en la lista de tus círculos. Para volver a esa lista después, haz clic en el nombre del círculo, arriba, y elige "Todos los círculos".
Usa el menú lateral para moverte entre Calendario, Medicamentos, Tareas, Notas, Signos vitales, Documentos, Miembros y más.
es.body:
## Qué puedes hacer en la computadora

Casi todo lo del día a día: ver el calendario, agregar y editar medicamentos, citas y tareas, marcar dosis, escribir notas, registrar signos vitales, subir documentos, mantener la información de emergencia, invitar a tu familia desde "Miembros" y administrar tus notificaciones y tu suscripción desde "Perfil". Lo que cambies aparece también en los celulares de todos.

## Qué necesita la app del celular

- **Recordatorios y alertas.** CircleCare los envía como notificaciones a la app de iPhone y Android. El sitio web no entrega recordatorios. Si quieres recibirlos, instala la app y activa las notificaciones. Consulta [No me llegan las notificaciones](/help/notifications-not-arriving/).
- **Agregar por voz** solo está en la app del celular.
- **Importar citas desde el calendario de tu celular** solo está en la app del celular.
- **Iniciar sesión con Face ID o huella** es una función del celular.

## Bueno saber

- Tus familiares invitados pueden unirse desde el navegador sin instalar nada. Sí necesitan una cuenta gratuita.
- Para cambiar de círculo en el sitio web, haz clic en el nombre del círculo, arriba, y luego en "Todos los círculos".

es.title: Agrega un medicamento y sus recordatorios
es.summary: Toca Nuevo, elige Medicamento, escribe el nombre, la dosis y los horarios, y guarda. Los recordatorios vienen activados, así que la persona indicada recibe aviso en cada toma.
steps: Toca Nuevo en la parte de abajo de la pantalla y luego Medicina.
Escribe el Nombre del medicamento y la Dosis (por ejemplo, 100mg o 1 tableta).
En Fecha y hora, elige una hora o toca un horario común como Cada mañana (también pone Repetir en Diario). Cuando ya hay una hora, toca Agregar otra dosis si se toma más de una vez al día (hasta 4).
En Repetir, elige cada cuánto se toma, como Diario o Días de la semana.
Revisa los Recordatorios. Activar notificaciones viene encendido, con A la hora programada marcado, y puedes sumar Recordatorios anticipados.
Toca Crear medicamento.
es.body:
## Lo que conviene saber

- **Quién recibe el recordatorio.** Los recordatorios de dosis le llegan a la persona que recibe el cuidado. Si el dueño del círculo eligió a alguien para encargarse de sus recordatorios de medicamentos, le llegan a esa persona. Consulta [Cómo funcionan los recordatorios y las alertas de dosis](/help/reminders-and-alerts/).
- **Más detalles** guarda las recargas, la farmacia, quien receta y las instrucciones. Activa **Seguimiento de recargas** para recibir aviso cuando el frasco se esté acabando.
- **Agregar una foto** del frasco ayuda a que todos confirmen la pastilla correcta.
- **Las horas son las de la zona horaria de la persona que recibe el cuidado.** Si vives en otro lugar, el formulario muestra tu hora y la suya.
- **Si la hora de hoy ya pasó**, el medicamento empieza con la próxima dosis. No se registra nada para hoy.
- **Agregar por voz.** En celulares compatibles, los círculos Premium pueden tocar **Agregar por voz** y decir el medicamento. El formulario se llena solo y no se guarda nada hasta que lo revises y confirmes.

## En la computadora

En [my.circlecare.app](/help/use-on-a-computer/), abre **Medicamentos** y elige **Agregar medicamento**. El formulario tiene los mismos campos. Los recordatorios son notificaciones push, así que solo llegan a celulares con la app de CircleCare instalada.

## Límites

- El plan gratuito no limita cuántos medicamentos ni recordatorios agregas.
- CircleCare es una herramienta, no un médico. No revisa interacciones entre medicamentos ni da indicaciones de dosis.

es.title: Medicamentos en ciertos días o cada pocos días
